info.title: OrbitID API
info.summary: Authentication, users, organizations, webhooks and OIDC for a self-hosted OrbitID instance.
info.description:
OrbitID exposes three surfaces on one origin.

- **Frontend API** (`/v1/client/*`): for browsers. Authenticated by the httpOnly `__client` cookie, which is
  created on first use. Never call it with a secret key.
- **Backend API** (`/v1/*`): for your servers. Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer sk_...` with the
  instance secret key. Responses include `private_metadata`.
- **OAuth/OIDC provider** (`/oauth/*`, `/.well-known/*`): standard endpoints for third-party clients.

All JSON is snake_case, all timestamps are Unix epoch **milliseconds**, and every id is prefixed with its
object type (`user_...`, `sess_...`, `org_...`). Errors use the envelope described by the `ApiError` schema,
except on the OAuth protocol endpoints, which answer with the standard `{ error, error_description }` shape.
List endpoints on the Backend API return `{ data, total_count }` and accept `limit`, `offset` and `order_by`.

Rate-limited endpoints answer `429` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Sensitive flows (sign-in,
sign-up, code verification, session-token minting) are limited per IP and per identifier.

get.description: Answers 200 when the process is up, with the publishable key and the database in use so a client can check that it is talking to the instance it expects. Intended for load balancers and container health checks.

Public projection of the instance settings that every UI component renders from: enabled factors, attribute requirements, organization settings and branding. Cacheable for 60 seconds; contains no secrets.

post.description: Creates a sign-in attempt for this client and advances it as far as the request allows. `status` says what is needed next: `needs_identifier`, `needs_first_factor`, `needs_second_factor`, `needs_new_password` or `complete` (with `created_session_id`). Starting an OAuth or enterprise SSO strategy returns `first_factor_verification.external_verification_redirect_url`; navigate the browser there. Failed password attempts count towards the user's lockout, and unknown identifiers return `form_identifier_not_found` unless enumeration protection is on. Rate limited per IP and identifier.

identifier.description: Email address, phone number or username. Required unless `strategy` is `oauth_*`, `enterprise_sso` or `ticket`.

strategy.description: First-factor strategy to start with: `password`, `email_code`, `email_link`, `phone_code`, `passkey`, `ticket`, `enterprise_sso` or `oauth_<provider>`.

ticket.description: One-time ticket from an actor token, a sign-in token or an invitation.

get.description: Lets a second tab or a polling page observe progress (for example after an email link was opened elsewhere).

post.description: Sends the email code, magic link or SMS code for the chosen strategy, or arms an OAuth redirect. The response carries the updated sign-in, so read `first_factor_verification` for the strategy state.
Verifies the password, code, passkey assertion or OAuth callback. Wrong codes and passwords return `form_code_incorrect` / `form_password_incorrect` and count towards the lockout. Rate limited.

signature.description: Signed message for a web3 strategy.

post.description: Sends an SMS code when the strategy is `phone_code`; `totp` and `backup_code` need no preparation.
Verifies a TOTP code, SMS code or single-use backup code. A completed sign-in returns `created_session_id`.

post.summary: Set a new password during sign-in
post.description: Completes the `needs_new_password` state, which is entered after a password-reset code was verified. The password policy is enforced. `sign_out_of_other_sessions` ends the user's other active sessions.

Creates an account attempt. The response's `missing_fields` and `unverified_fields` are computed from the instance's attribute settings; fill them in with `PATCH` and verify identifiers with `prepare_verification`/`attempt_verification`. Sign-up completes (`status: complete`, `created_session_id` set) as soon as nothing is missing. Sign-up is gated by the instance's sign-up mode, the allow/block lists and invitation tickets. Rate limited per IP.

post.description: Starts an OAuth flow. The response contains a placeholder external account whose `verification.external_verification_redirect_url` is where the browser must go; the return path is `redirect_url`. Requires a recent first-factor verification.

post.description: Returns the base32 secret, the `otpauth://` URI and a QR code data URL **once**. Confirm with `attempt_verification`.

Signs a short-lived (60 s) RS256 JWT for the session, optionally with a JWT template. The browser SDK calls this about every 50 s and writes the result to `__session`. Rate limited to 300 calls per minute per client.

post.description: Same as `createSessionToken` with the template in the path. Unknown templates return 404.

Starts a reverification for endpoints that need a recent factor (profile changes, deleting the account, revoking devices). Read `response.verification` for the next step. Endpoints that need reverification answer `session_reverification_required` with `meta.levels`.

get.description: Minutes since the session's first and second factor were verified (`-1` when never), which is what the SDK's reverification hook uses to decide whether a fresh factor is needed.

response.description: Minutes since each factor was verified; `-1` when never.

get.summary: Read the session signing keys (legacy path)

Standard authorization code flow. PKCE (`S256`) is required for public clients. Without a session the browser is sent to the app's sign-in page and brought back; with consent enabled the consent screen data comes from `/oauth/consent_info`. Ends in a redirect carrying `code` and `state`, or `error` and `error_description`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Must match a registered redirect URI exactly.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space separated. `openid` is required for OIDC.

get.description: Application name, requested scopes and descriptions for the consent screen.

post.description: Records the grant for this user and application and returns where to send the browser next.

Exchanges an authorization code or a refresh token for an access token, and (with the `openid` scope) an id_token. Confidential clients authenticate with HTTP Basic (`client_id:client_secret`) or with `client_id` and `client_secret` in the body. Errors use the OAuth error shape, not the OrbitID error envelope.

get.description: OIDC userinfo for the access token in `Authorization: Bearer` (or `?access_token=`).

post.description: Same claims as the GET form, for clients that must not put tokens in a URL.
RFC 7009. Answers 200 with an empty body whether or not the token existed.
RFC 7662. Returns `active: false` for unknown, expired or revoked tokens.

post.summary: Mint a machine token with client credentials
post.description: `client_credentials` grant for a machine: `machine_id` + `machine_secret` (body or HTTP Basic). Equivalent to `POST /v1/m2m/tokens` without the secret key, so a machine can mint its own tokens.
`client_secret` is returned once, in this response. Public clients get no secret and must use PKCE.

scopes.description: Space separated scopes. Defaults to `openid profile email`.

image_url.description: Profile image URL, or a generated initials image.

private_metadata.description: Backend API only. Never returned by the Frontend API.

actor.description: Set when a Backend API actor token created the session during impersonation.

factor_verification_age.description: Minutes since the first and the second factor were verified; `-1` when never.

SignInFactor.description: One way the user can satisfy a sign-in step.

role.description: Role key, for example `org:admin` or a custom `org:billing`.

url.description: Invitation link. Backend API only, and only when no email was sent.
Invitation link, returned when the email was not sent.

signing_key.description: Verification key for templates with a custom signing key: an HS256 secret or a public JWK.

actor.description: Claims copied into the session's `act` claim.

token.description: One-time token, returned only from the creating request.
One-time token, returned only from the creating request.

secret.description: `whsec_…` signing secret. Returned on create, on rotate and from `GET …/secret` only.
`ak_live_…` secret. Returned once, when the key is created.

token.description: Opaque `mt_…` token or JWT, returned only from the creating request.

client_secret.description: Returned on create and on secret rotation only.

scopes.description: Space separated scopes granted to the application.

secret.description: Base32 secret, returned once during setup.

qr_code.description: `data:` URL of a QR code for the URI.

identification_requirements.description: One entry per accepted identifier combination.

social.description: Enabled social providers keyed by provider name.

Instance.description: Instance settings. Secret values (`smtpUrl`, `twilioAuthToken`, `captchaSecret`, social `clientSecret`) are returned as `••••` together with a sibling `<field>Set` boolean; send the tree back without the masked values to keep the stored secrets.

items.description: JSON Web Key. RSA keys carry `n`/`e`; EC keys carry `x`/`y`/`crv`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

UserInfo.description: Claims for the user behind the access token: `sub`, and whichever of `email`, `email_verified`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `picture` the scopes allow.

message.description: Short human-readable message, safe to show to the end user.

long_message.description: Longer explanation with the fix, when there is one.

errors.description: One entry per problem; a single request can report several validation errors.

trace_id.description: Correlation id for the request. Include it when reporting a problem.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read: malformed JSON, an unparsable body or an invalid query parameter.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials. The Frontend API also answers this when the client cookie is gone.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed. The Frontend API also returns this for a pending session that still has to enrol a second factor (`session_pending`), and for missing organization permissions.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or it belongs to someone else.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with existing state: a duplicate record, an already accepted invitation, or the last admin.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed on the request body or query. `meta.param_name` names the offending field.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait, and `errors[0].code` is `rate_limit_exceeded`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next attempt is allowed.

OAuthBadRequest.description: The request is malformed or an OAuth parameter is missing; `error` names the RFC 6749 code.

OAuthUnauthorized.description: Client authentication failed (`invalid_client`), or the bearer token is missing or invalid.

OrderBy.name: order_by
OrderBy.description: Sort field, prefixed with `-` for descending (`-created_at`) or `+` for ascending. An unknown field falls back to the endpoint's default order.

Paginated.name: paginated
Paginated.description: When `true`, the response is `{ data, total_count }` instead of the plain envelope.

SecretKey.description: Instance secret key (`sk_live_...` / `sk_test_...`) as `Authorization: Bearer sk_...`. Grants full Backend API access, so it must only ever be used from a server you control.

ClientCookie.name: __client
ClientCookie.description: Opaque client token set by `GET /v1/client` as an httpOnly cookie. One per browser or device.

SessionToken.description: Session JWT (RS256, 60 s lifetime) minted by `POST /v1/client/sessions/{id}/tokens`.

OAuth2.description: Access token issued by this instance's `/oauth/token` endpoint for an OAuth application.

scopes.email: Email address and whether it is verified.

scopes.machine:token: Mint tokens as a machine identity.

MachineSecret.description: Machine secret from `POST /v1/m2m/machines`. Only `/oauth/m2m/token` accepts it.
